title: Google Health is ending pairing support for older Fitbit scales on November 28
summary: The hardware lives on, but its second chance at syncing won't.
body: TL;DR Google is ending pairing and re-pairing support for Fitbit Aria and Aria 2 smart scales on November 28, 2026. Some owners are already unable to connect their scales, despite the official deadline still being days away. Previously paired scales will continue syncing, but disconnecting them could mean losing automatic weight tracking for good. Smart home gadgets have a habit of outliving the software that makes them smart. A device can work perfectly well for years, only to lose some of its most useful features when its manufacturer decides it’s time to move on. That’s the frustration facing some longtime Fitbit Aria smart scales, which are approaching a deadline that could leave them stuck with little more than ordinary bathroom scales. Starting November 28, 2026 , Google will stop supporting new pairing and re-pairing for the Fitbit Aria and Aria 2 smart scales. The change is tied to Google Health version 5.12, although the app has already moved past that release, with version 5.13 now rolling out .

title: Google explains the 6GB RAM and 10GB storage demands for its new 3D emoji
summary: The numbers make more sense now.
body: TL;DR Google’s new 3D emoji don’t actually require 10GB of storage or consume 6GB of RAM. The 3D font occupies less than 220MB, while the listed hardware requirements are safeguards for automatic downloads. Google hasn’t clarified whether users can opt out of downloading the new emoji. Google’s new Noto 3D emoji were supposed to give Android a fresh look, but their surprisingly demanding hardware requirements have left some users scratching their heads. After all, why should a new set of emoji require 6GB of RAM and 10GB of free storage? While Google’s support page also confirmed that Samsung phones won’t receive the new designs , the hardware requirements sparked another debate, prompting Google to step in with an explanation. The good news? The new emoji don’t actually consume 6GB of RAM or 10GB of storage. According to Google’s Mishaal Rahman (via Reddit ), who verified the details with the emoji design team, the entire 3D font takes up less than 220MB. That’s considerably larger than the roughly 3MB used by the older 2D emoji, but nowhere near 10GB.

The experimental app supports typing indicators, read receipts, reactions, and media and file sharing. The initial implementation will still depend on sandboxed Google Play, but won’t require Google Messages. The eventual goal is a standalone implementation for supported carriers. The RCS functionality will effectively be exclusive to GrapheneOS. GrapheneOS is making progress on one of its most anticipated messaging features, and it could eventually let users enjoy RCS without relying on Google Messages.

title: Molly Meldrum, Australian Music Broadcaster and ‘Countdown’ Host, Dies at 83
summary: "Affectionately dubbed 'The Guru,' Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music," his family said in a statement.
body: Ian “Molly” Meldrum, the Australian broadcaster, journalist and record producer whose weekly television show made stars of international and local acts alike, died Monday (Nov. 23) at Epworth Hospital in Richmond, Melbourne. He was 83. His family said he died peacefully after a long period of ill health. “Affectionately dubbed ‘The Guru,’ Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music,” they said in a statement. “He shaped not only the sound of a nation but also the dreams of generations who grew up with his voice guiding them.” He is survived by his long-term partner, Yan Wongngam. From 1974 to 1987, Meldrum presented Countdown , the ABC’s Sunday-evening music program, which he co-created with executive producer Michael Shrimpton and producer-director Robbie Weekes. Across 563 episodes, it became appointment viewing for young Australians, and — years before MTV — a showcase that leaned heavily on music video.
